### 📓 Docs Drift Check
**6** anchor(s) derived from **1** changed package(s); no hand-written page names any of them. ⚠️ **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/plugins/plugin-email/vitest.config.ts`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/plugins/plugin-email/vitest.config.ts`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **7** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json e3f0cfd422d69100448ccd4f6a329c90a25715f7` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `04d65c18570b5d951f535bc4b833a2c0f7690528` — the merge of head `019a4f028dfde8b27a1fe504404b492bbb5cf29f` into base `e3f0cfd422d69100448ccd4f6a329c90a25715f7`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 04d65c18570b5d951f535bc4b833a2c0f7690528 && git checkout 04d65c18570b5d951f535bc4b833a2c0f7690528
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin e3f0cfd422d69100448ccd4f6a329c90a25715f7 019a4f028dfde8b27a1fe504404b492bbb5cf29f && git checkout -B drift-repro e3f0cfd422d69100448ccd4f6a329c90a25715f7 && git merge --no-ff 019a4f028dfde8b27a1fe504404b492bbb5cf29f

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json e3f0cfd422d69100448ccd4f6a329c90a25715f7
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `4419624c1a5eab1741ba6f47502180d001bd6b93`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/plugins/plugin-email/src/template-loader.ts, .changeset/32670-email-send-served-holders.md + packages/plugins/plugin-email/src/template-loader.test.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-email/vitest.config.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-email/package.json, scripts/engine-double-contract.pinned.json, docs/adr/0150 (D3, D4)

### ① Derived judgments

- **The nothing-disabled path is main's.** `bundleAddressOf` computes `holders` (all, built-ins filtered) and `served` (without `includeDisabledPackages`), and branches only when `served.length < holders.length`. Otherwise the code is main's: the old inline `shared` registry is now `withoutCallerHolding(scoped, { includeDisabledPackages: true })`, the same object. The probe reports 0 of 31,104 answers moved with nothing disabled. That satisfies the red line "one-holder behaviour unchanged" for every enabled composition.
- **`servedBundleAddressOf`.** It resolves over the served holders only, so a refusal names only serving packages (rows 29–30) and a disabled package is never the answer:
  - resolved to a served package: that package's own address, the same list main already used for a two-holder name;
  - resolved to a package that is not served: only reachable when the caller's own holding is the disabled one, and it answers `NO_BUNDLE` (row 36);
  - not resolved: `NO_BUNDLE` (rows 31, 37);
  - an addition-only caller, or the built-ins: re-resolved from the caller's closure over the served holders, and read only at the built-ins' address or a served holder's address (rows 29, 38).
  Every answer that can carry a member is a package-own or built-ins address. The environment-wide list is never read while a disabled holder exists, except on the environment-item branch.
- **Choosing the address rather than filtering after the read** is justified: the execution list's `_packageId` is the slot an item fills, not where it is stored. A post-read filter on it would either leak a pair row or drop a dependent's locale. This is the only way to meet the member rule of 6819947096 until #32354 lands. Measured: out-of-rule sends drop from 1,127 to 107, none new, and all 107 are the unmoved R4-F nothing-disabled shape.
- nit N1: the environment-item branch (`resolved.holder.kind !== 'package'` → `undefined`, the environment-wide read) is unreachable in the matrix, because the registry answers no environment item for a name any package holds. If it ever became reachable, it is the one branch that would read the environment-wide list beside a disabled holder. `NO_BUNDLE` there would make "no disabled side member is ever read" hold by construction instead of by reachability. This is optional, since the author keeps main's answer deliberately.
- **Pins.** 11 cases × 2 orders × 2 reads (protocol real list and registry list) × 9 callers × 2 locales. Built on a real `SchemaRegistry` and the real `getMetaItemsForExecution` over stored rows, with no double over `listItems`; the `findOne` double is pinned in the engine-double ledger (+1 row). Each ablation (A1, A2, A4, A5, A6) turns its rows red, and A3 was measured as dead code and deleted.

### ② Semver level

`@objectstack/plugin-email: patch`, `fix(plugin-email)!`, `Clause-②: yes (narrowing)` with the widening rows in prose, a BREAKING paragraph, and one `adr-0087: not-required (no-migration-prescription)` marker. Correct for a non-protocol narrowing (AGENTS.md). `Metadata-protocol: none` and `Skills-docs: none — reason` hold.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **Landing waits on E1's #32354** (no PR yet), as the card orders. Until then the disabled side stays listed in the environment-wide and base-scoped lists, which is why this PR chooses addresses. Once #32354 lands, the "separate, declared move" the body mentions is owed.
- Out of scope and with the seat for a ruling: the `_env` cell of #32183 row 17 (needs `packages/metadata-protocol/**`, area E1) and the R4-G flow doors. Neither is in this diff.
- Shared baseline `scripts/engine-double-contract.pinned.json` (+5, one ledger row) and a test-only workspace devDependency `@objectstack/metadata-protocol` plus a vitest source alias. `metadata-protocol` does not depend on `plugin-email`, so there is no cycle.
- CI at this head when read (18:14Z): 58 success, 9 skipped, none red. The author reports the local dogfood battery green (464/467 files). The ACCEPT cites it and re-reads every check at the landing head.

### ④ Design judgment

**Row 37, as asked: accepted as declared (no template).** Under ADR-0150 D4, an environment item or package-less row for a name a package holds is that package's customization. The registry already answers it that way (`getEnvironmentScopedItem` is undefined for a held name, and the execution list stamps the item with the holder's slot). A dependent's addition and the pair row also belong to the holder's side. When the only holder is disabled, its whole side, customization included, holds no name at the send (D3 as ruled on #32183). Serving the environment's item there would treat a customization as an independent environment item, which would loosen resolution and depend on the disable state in a way D4 does not provide. Withholding it is reversible: re-enabling the package restores the same answer. This is a judgment on a declared row, not a new seat ruling. If the seat wants the opposite answer, that would be a behaviour-changing ADR interpretation and needs its Fable pass.

The rest holds: judging the send over the served holders completes D3 at the last door #32183 left at main (R4-A). Choosing the address over filtering is forced by what the execution list carries, and it keeps the member rule.
